def count_lis_lds_permutations(n, a, b):
    """Count permutations of {1, ..., n} whose longest strictly increasing
    subsequence has length exactly a AND whose longest strictly decreasing
    subsequence has length exactly b.

    Input domain: integers with 1 <= n <= 40, 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n.
    (n is capped at 40; brute-force enumeration of n! permutations is
    astronomically infeasible there, so a structural insight is required.)

    Returns the exact count as a Python int (possibly enormous; exact
    integer arithmetic required, no floating point). Returns 0 whenever no
    permutation satisfies the constraints (for example when a * b < n, or
    when a + b - 1 > n).

    Subsequences need not be contiguous. "Exactly" means exactly: a
    permutation with a longer increasing subsequence than a, or a longer
    decreasing subsequence than b, is not counted.

    Examples:

    >>> count_lis_lds_permutations(3, 2, 2)
    4
    >>> count_lis_lds_permutations(4, 2, 2)
    4
    >>> count_lis_lds_permutations(6, 3, 2)
    25
    >>> count_lis_lds_permutations(10, 3, 3)
    0
    """
